subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage: I sat on the park bench watching a toddler named Uday explore near the slide, and I noticed something. Every few minutes he stopped, turned and looked for his mother Pallavi on the next bench. She lifted a hand; he grinned and toddled off again. Once he ran back, patted her knee and left. I can't know what he felt, but he seemed to use her as a home base. When he wandered towards the gate, Pallavi stood up and walked over to him.

qa.q: Where was Pallavi sitting?
qa.a: On the next bench in the park.

qa.q: What does the narrator think Uday's looking back shows?
qa.a: The narrator thinks he wanted reassurance that his mother was still there, using her as a base, and does not claim to know what he felt.

qa.q: Why did Pallavi stand up when Uday went toward the gate?
qa.a: He was heading somewhere less safe, and at his age he needs an adult to watch and step in. She might also just want to keep him within sight.

qa.q: How might Pallavi feel as she watches him roam and return?
qa.a: She may feel proud that he explores and glad that he checks in, while staying alert to danger.

grounding: A toddler stays within sight of a parent, returns for reassurance and explores, seen by an observer, with the parent supervising near the gate.

subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage: Monday: at the park, Mehak, two, stayed close to Sonali's bench, digging in the sand within arm's reach, glancing up now and then. Tuesday: she walked to the slide and looked back three times, waiting for Sonali's nod before climbing. Wednesday: she ran further, laughing, then hurried back for a quick hug and dashed off again. Then she headed straight for the gate without looking back, so Sonali quickly moved beside her and took her hand. “Let's explore this way.”

qa.q: What did Mehak do on Tuesday before climbing the slide?
qa.a: She looked back at Sonali several times and waited for her nod.

qa.q: What might Mehak's looking back and quick hug mean she felt?
qa.a: They suggest she wanted reassurance and feels safe with Sonali, which lets her explore further. It might also be simple habit.

qa.q: Why did Sonali step in on Wednesday?
qa.a: Mehak headed to the gate without checking back, so she needed supervision to stay safe.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel over these three days?
qa.a: Sonali may feel glad and proud as Mehak grows braver, and watchful as the distances grow. 🙂

grounding: A toddler stays near a caregiver, returns for reassurance and explores further, and a child who wanders off without checking back needs supervision.

subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage: At the Lodhi Garden lawn in Delhi, Dolma toddled off toward the flowerbed. Halfway there, she stopped and looked back at Devika, her nanny, on the bench. Devika waved. Dolma ran back, patted Devika's knee once, then set off again, farther this time, to the fountain. She looked back again. Another wave. This time she didn't come back, just smiled and kept watching the water.

qa.q: Where did Dolma go the second time?
qa.a: To the fountain.

qa.q: Why did Dolma keep looking back at Devika?
qa.a: She wanted to check Devika was still there, which made her feel safe enough to explore farther; she seemed confident and happy.

qa.q: What could Devika keep doing to support Dolma's exploring?
qa.a: Stay in sight, wave back each time Dolma checks, and keep watch as Dolma goes farther.

qa.q: How might Devika feel as Dolma explores farther?
qa.a: She probably feels pleased at Dolma's growing confidence, while keeping a close eye on her near the water.

grounding: A toddler explores away from her nanny and checks back for reassurance, showing trust and safe-base seeking.

subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage:
"Santosh, where's Kunal?"
"There, by the bangle stall. He keeps coming back to touch my leg, then off again."
"Good. He's checking on us."
"Now he's going round the corner."
"Did he look back?"
"No. Not once."
"Go. Now."
Santosh walked quickly after him and scooped Kunal up by the balloon cart. "You went too far, little one. Stay where you can see Papa."
Kunal laughed and pointed at the balloons.

qa.q: Where did Santosh scoop Kunal up?
qa.a: By the balloon cart.

qa.q: What might Kunal have been feeling when he went round the corner without looking back?
qa.a: He was probably excited and curious about the stalls and not worried at all, which is why he stopped checking back.

qa.q: Why did Santosh go after him quickly?
qa.a: Because Kunal had stopped looking back, which meant he needed close supervision in the crowd.

qa.q: How might Kunal's mother have felt when he went round the corner?
qa.a: She was likely worried and alarmed, which is why she told Santosh to go at once.

grounding: Parents notice their toddler's checking back and act quickly when he wanders off without it, since he needs supervision.

subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage: Childminder's note, Wednesday. At the park Sunaina did her usual loop: out to the sandpit, back to touch my knee, out to the swings, back again. Around mid-morning she walked toward the gate and did not look back once. I followed her straight away and brought her back to the sandpit. She was happy, not upset. I will stay closer when she is near the gate, as she doesn't seem to check when she gets excited. Bhavna, childminder

qa.q: What did Sunaina do each time she came back?
qa.a: She came back to touch the childminder's knee.

qa.q: What was Sunaina likely feeling when she walked toward the gate?
qa.a: She was probably curious and excited, and in that mood she forgot to check back, rather than trying to run off.

qa.q: What did Bhavna plan to do differently?
qa.a: To stay closer when Sunaina is near the gate, since she doesn't check back when excited.

qa.q: How might Sunaina's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They would likely feel reassured that Bhavna noticed quickly and has a plan to keep her safe.

grounding: A childminder notes a toddler's pattern of returning for reassurance and supervises closely when she wanders off without checking.

subtype: Approaching and staying near a caregiver [Expressing]
passage:
The church feast in the Kerala village filled the lane with drums and balloon sellers. Jomon toddled towards a balloon stall, stopped, and looked back at his Amma, Deepika.
She waved. He trotted back, touched her knee, and set off again.
Then a crowd swallowed him and he went round the back of a stall without looking back once.
Deepika was after him in three steps. She caught his hand. “Stay where you can see me.”

qa.q: What was filling the lane at the church feast?
qa.a: Drums and balloon sellers filled the lane.

qa.q: What does Jomon touching Deepika's knee and setting off again suggest he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt safe and reassured by her, then brave enough to explore again.

qa.q: Why was Deepika right to follow Jomon quickly?
qa.a: Once he stopped checking back and disappeared in a crowd, he needed close watching, so she caught his hand.

qa.q: What is it like for Deepika when Jomon vanishes behind the stall?
qa.a: She would feel a jolt of fear and act fast to reach him.

grounding: It shows a toddler exploring and returning to a parent for reassurance, and the parent supervising when he wanders off without checking back.
